source.toolchain: microsoft/vega-prover rev c0ee259, zk-cred-vega setup() (sirosfoundation/zk-cred-vega commit 246eee9)

notes: Fixes a real under-constraint found while scoping an independent security review: digest_id_extract's value-byte mapping is right-aligned, so for CBOR uint length classes 0/1/2 the high-order bytes of the exposed digestID were free witness variables, and both range checks went vacuous (gated by a different class's selector). A prover generating its own witness could select class 1 to match real bytes 0x18 0x1A (digestID 26) while exposing 0x0ABBCC1A -- defeating the digestID-to-claim-bytes binding r6 was meant to establish. Fixed by constraining every value byte the selected class does not encode to zero, per-class, with a regression test that tampers with the witness directly (verified to fail without the fix). Likely fail-safe rather than forgeable (a conformant verifier rejects), but it broke the intended guarantee. Supersedes r6 (deprecated). Still unpublished -- sha256_var/mso_splice/onehot_cursor/digest_id_extract remain unreviewed (see REVIEW-SCOPE.md), on top of the pre-existing ECDSA range-check gap.
